CONFIRMED BY READING BEFORE IMPLEMENTING and accepted as the orchestrator framed it: the rejection path is the one nobody in the field is on yet, and the legacy path is the one a real Memex/consumer database hits on upgrade — under-covering it in exactly the two SDKs consumers use is the wrong asymmetry, and X1 parity is a release gate, not a follow-up. Both bindings now seed the legacy `{filterable} + fts + vector` registry row through a raw SQLite INSERT on `_fathomdb_projection_registry` (`_seed_legacy_registry_row` in Python, `seedLegacyRegistryRow` in TS, mirroring the Rust `seed_legacy_registry_row` column-for-column, same encoding — `fts_tokenizer = ''` is an `fts` sub-object with the DEFAULT tokenizer, NULL is no sub-object) and assert the SAME three oracles as Rust: (a) `read.projections` reports the row VERBATIM (name, roles = {filterable}, fts, vector), (b) feeding that output straight back into `configure_projections` raises `WriteValidationError` / `FDB_WRITE_VALIDATION` — the shipped fix-4 read→configure round-trip, broken by design for this population, (c) adding the `searchable` role is the remedy and the rest of the declaration is untouched. LEG 2 / TC-90 (seq-128, p1) — CHARACTERIZED, REPRODUCES 10/10, NO FIX. The ledger claim is CORRECT on the code: `Engine::transition` opens `connection.transaction()` (rusqlite BEGIN DEFERRED, lib.rs:8221), reads first (`SELECT state, write_cursor, body FROM canonical_nodes ...`, lib.rs:8229) and writes second (`UPDATE canonical_nodes SET state = ?1 ...`, lib.rs:8259) — structurally identical to commit_batch's pre-TC-57-fix shape. What it ALSO has, and commit_batch did not, are two mitigations: a `drain(30s)` before the transaction (lib.rs:8217) and the shared writer-connection mutex (lib.rs:8219, same mutex write_inner takes at lib.rs:5051). Those narrow the in-process window to the gap between `drain` returning and the mutex being acquired. MEASURED at 94f09d7d, N=10 per arm: stress repro (2 writer threads x 24-row bursts, 1 ms pace, 0 ms embed) 10/10 FAILED, mean 5.9 EngineError::Storage per 40 transitions = 14.8 %, scheduler_errors 0 and other_errors 0 in every run; stress control (identical load, no vector kind ⇒ no second writer) 0/10 with embed_calls 0.

LEG 2 / TC-90 — THE NEGATIVE THAT WAS NEARLY FILED. The TC-57-shaped PACED arm (1 writer, 1 row per write, 3 ms pace, 2 ms embed) is 0/10 over 1200 transitions with a live worker, and its control is 0/10. Reporting only that arm would have been a clean, well-measured, completely FALSE negative. The governing parameter is the EMBED DELAY: the worker cannot hold the write lock until at least one embed latency after the competing write released the connection mutex, whereas `transition` travels from acquiring that mutex to its promoting UPDATE in microseconds. Setting embed delay to 0 collapses the offset and the defect appears 10/10. General lesson recorded in the doc §2.4: a 0/10 at one load shape is not evidence of absence — name the parameter that governs the window and vary THAT.

LEG 2 / TC-90 — MECHANISM CAPTURED, NOT ASSUMED (the TC-57 §0 lesson applied). `transition` is WORSE than commit_batch on the error path: it maps every rusqlite error through `.map_err(|_| EngineError::Storage)` and never calls `emit_sqlite_internal_error`, so the numeric code is not merely opaque to the host — it is never produced, and no lifecycle sink can capture it. The mechanism was therefore pinned DETERMINISTICALLY by holding the write lock rather than racing for it. `tc90_mechanism_transition_sql_shape_on_real_schema_is_busy_5` replays transition's two statements character-for-character against a REAL engine-created `canonical_nodes`, with a 5 s busy timeout and a counting busy handler installed: primary=DatabaseBusy, EXTENDED code = 5 (plain SQLITE_BUSY, NOT SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT/517), busy handler invoked ZERO times, returned in 0 ms. Identical to TC-57's Exit B. A fix scoped to retrying 517 would ship INERT here too. 517 never observed; treated as reachable-but-unobserved, same as TC-57 §2.4.

LEG 2 / TC-90 — DOES TC-57's R1 (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) TRANSFER? MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, as the brief required. Two pins apply the IDENTICAL contention (one external connection holding the WAL write lock) and differ only in which engine entry point is called: `Engine::transition` (BEGIN DEFERRED, read-then-upgrade) returns Err(Storage) in 0 ms; `Engine::write` (already BEGIN IMMEDIATE since Slice 21a-2, lib.rs:18637) WAITS 834 ms for the lock and SUCCEEDS. Same database, same contention, same 5 000 ms default busy timeout, opposite outcomes. That is direct evidence the remedy is applicable — but §7 R-A also records the measured reason it is NOT free: making the engine the lock holder more often is exactly the input that drives TC-91's worker-side commit loss, so R-A alone could reduce TC-90 while INCREASING TC-91 duplicates. Enumerated, not implemented.

LEG 2 / TC-90 — A SECOND, DISTINCT DEFECT FOUND WHILE BOUNDING AN ARM, recorded and NOT folded into TC-90. At fully saturating load (writer_pace_ms 0) `transition`'s own `drain` NEVER reaches idle: in 181 seconds the loop issued 5 transitions of which 4 failed with EngineError::Scheduler, each having burned the full LIFECYCLE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS (30 s), while 596,928 competing rows landed. This is an AVAILABILITY property of the drain-then-act design, not the promote race: under sustained write pressure a lifecycle verb can be starved indefinitely, one 30-second timeout at a time, and the caller sees an opaque Scheduler error. `configure_projections` (lib.rs:8332), `purge` (lib.rs:8441/8443) and the verb at lib.rs:8646-8648 take the same drain-first path and are PRESUMED to share it — NOT measured, flagged. The shipped arms use writer_pace_ms 1 so drain can still reach idle, hence scheduler_errors 0 across all 10 stress runs.

LEG 2 / TC-91 (a) (seq-129, p2) — THE ~50 % BASELINE DUPLICATE RATE, CONFIRMED AT HEAD WITH THE PROBE CONTRIBUTION SEPARATED. Definition counted: every row carries a UNIQUE body, the embedder records the exact `text` of every embed() call, and a duplicate is an embed call beyond the FIRST for any single text — a count, not an inference from a total. MEASURED N=10 per arm at 94f09d7d: governed (logical_id: Some) 102-106 duplicates over 200 rows, mean 104.0 = 52.0 %; anonymous (logical_id: None) 103-110, mean 105.0 = 52.5 %. Indistinguishable (0.5 pp apart, inside spread), and the anonymous path has no read-then-upgrade window at all — so the ledger claim that this is NOT the TC-57 race is CONFIRMED. In all 20 runs ingest_distinct == 200, vector_rows == 200, up_to_date_terminals == 200, failed_terminals == 0, failure_audit_rows == 0.

LEG 2 / TC-91 (a) — THE MEASUREMENT TRAP, DISARMED FIRST AND VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Two defences, both mechanical: (i) every duplicate arm runs inside a SINGLE open of a fresh workspace whose embed log starts empty — `_fathomdb_vector_kinds` is empty at open so `run_vector_equivalence_probe` returns early (lib.rs:15348-15353) having embedded nothing, and the kind is enrolled AFTER open; (ii) every body carries the marker `tc91marker` which no probe text contains, ingest and probe embeds are counted separately and NEVER summed, and EVERY duplicate arm asserts `probe_calls == 0` so a broken separation fails the arm instead of silently contaminating the number. Measured probe contribution: 0 in all 20 duplicate runs.

LEG 2 / TC-91 — A STALE FIGURE THIS REPO CARRIES, CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT AT HEAD. The ledger note describing 45 probe re-embeds on every open PREDATES TC-68's landing in Slice 22 (572475f2), so it was not inherited as a constant. `tc91_probe_embed_cost_per_open_at_head` measures three consecutive opens of one workspace as DELTAS (per seq-125: absolute embed counts are unusable as an oracle across a reopen): open 1 (fresh, no vector kind) = 0; open 2 (vector kind present, probe table empty ⇒ populate 45 + check 45) = 90; open 3 (TC-68 fingerprint verdict cache live) = 0. TC-68 took the steady-state reopen probe cost to ZERO, not merely reduced it. The 90 on the population open is unchanged and still must be subtracted; the 45-per-open figure is NO LONGER TRUE for any open after that. The test asserts open3 < open2 rather than == 0, so an unrelated fingerprint change does not read as a defect.

LEG 2 / TC-91 (b) — THE SILENTLY DISCARDED WORKER COMMIT, LOCATED, QUOTED AND PROVEN BLIND BY A FORCED-FAILURE EXPERIMENT. Call sites: `let _ = commit_projection_outcomes(connection, &outcomes, shared);` at lib.rs:12711 (run_projection_jobs) and lib.rs:12824 (commit_projection_panic_failures). Both discard a rusqlite::Result<()> — no error, no log, no telemetry, no counter. THE DURABLE POINT: a 'failed' terminal and a projection_failures audit row are written ONLY by the ProjectionOutcome::Failure arm (lib.rs:13962-13984), which represents an EMBED failure; a COMMIT failure never reaches that arm at all — the transaction rolls back, the row keeps terminal IS NULL, the worker sets pending_scan = true (lib.rs:12663), the dispatcher re-fetches and the row is embedded AGAIN. Therefore COUNTING 'failed' TERMINAL STATES IS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF SEEING THIS FAILURE CLASS, because the failure never reaches a terminal state at all; any future attempt to quantify worker reliability that way reports a FALSELY CLEAN ZERO no matter how many commits are lost. PROVEN by holding the WAL write lock from an ordinary second connection (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) for 1 500 ms over a 96-row batch: N=10, duplicate embeds 80-96 (mean 86.4, ~90 %), 32 distinct rows re-embedded in EVERY run, while failed_terminals == 0 AND failure_audit_rows == 0 in EVERY run. vector_rows == 96 throughout — this is WASTED WORK and an OBSERVABILITY hole, not data loss. The test asserts the blindness (counters zero WHILE duplicates non-zero), so a green run means work was computed, thrown away, recomputed, and the terminal census reported a perfectly clean run.

LEG 2 / TC-91 — MECHANISM IDENTIFIED: (a) IS (b), DRIVEN BY THE ENGINE'S OWN WRITER. `tc91_mechanism_duplicate_rate_versus_write_cadence` runs the same 60 governed rows twice varying ONLY the spacing between Engine::write calls: tight (1 ms) = 31-33 duplicates, mean 32.5 = 54.2 %; spaced (25 ms) = 0 in all 10 runs. The §5.4 control (one 96-row batch, no concurrent writer) is also 0. So a duplicate REQUIRES a second writer holding the WAL write lock across the worker's commit: commit_batch holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE (lib.rs:18637, the TC-57 fix) for the duration of every write, while commit_projection_outcomes (lib.rs:13809) is a DEFERRED read-then-upgrade (reads at :13813 and :13828 before its writes at :13863), so when they overlap the worker's promotion is refused with plain SQLITE_BUSY and `let _ =` discards the outcome. THE ~50 % IS A PROPERTY OF THE WRITE CADENCE, NOT A CONSTANT OF THE SCHEDULER — quoting it without the cadence it was measured at is not meaningful. This also closes TC-57 §7 uncertainty 3 in a direction that document could not see: its §8.2 measured worker pressure only RELATIVELY (before vs after the caller-side fix) and had no no-concurrency baseline, so it could not show that the ~104/200 it recorded as 'pre-existing' was already this defect.

LEG 2 / TC-91 (c) — TC-57 REMEDY R2 CARRIED FORWARD IN THE DOC ONLY, as instructed. R2 (bounded retry on the busy codes in the caller path) remains UNIMPLEMENTED pending the error-path restructure it depends on (commit_batch's rusqlite::Error is discarded at lib.rs:5096-5099, so there is nothing to branch on). R1 shipped and closed the measured defect, so R2 is AN OPTION, NOT AN OBLIGATION (TC-57 §8.4). TC-90 does not change that verdict but adds one data point: transition's error path is WORSE than commit_batch's (no lifecycle event at all), so if the restructure is ever undertaken transition should be in its scope. Recorded as R-E, lower priority than R-A/R-B/R-C, not recommended for 0.8.21 on its own.

fix-2 FINDING 1 [measurement-trust] (codex §9 round 4) — the TC-90 stress-arm non-vacuity assertions were too weak to defend the protocol. `tc90_transition_write_race.rs:599` asserted only `attempted > 0` and `storage_errors == 0`; it did NOT assert `attempted == STRESS_TRANSITIONS`, `truncated == false`, `scheduler_errors == 0` or `other_errors == 0`. CONFIRMED BY READING: a run that issued ONE transition, or truncated at its wall-clock budget, or was dominated by `Scheduler` drain timeouts, would have satisfied the eventual 0.8.21 green bar (design doc §4) WITHOUT ever measuring the 40-transition promote race the doc documents at characterization line 168. The numbers were in the report but not in the code. FIX: a new shared `assert_protocol_ran(outcome, expected_transitions)` pinning `attempted == transitions`, `truncated == false`, `competing_writes > 0`, `scheduler_errors == 0`, `other_errors == 0`. Applied to ALL FOUR arms, not only the two codex named — the PACED pair asserted no `Scheduler`/`other` counts either, so the same weakness existed there and generalizing the helper was the smaller change than fixing half of it. Deliberate consequence recorded at `ArmConfig::budget` and in design doc §2.1: the budget becomes a safety valve whose USE IS A FAILURE, not a licence to measure less. RE-MEASURED N=10/arm after tightening (session B): stress repro 10/10 reproduce with `attempted=40 truncated=false scheduler_errors=0 other_errors=0` in every run and the failure landing on the `storage_errors` oracle (i.e. every protocol assertion passed first); stress control 0/10; paced repro 0/10; paced control 0/10. NO assertion was loosened.

fix-2 FINDING 4 [OVERCLAIM — the important one] (codex §9 round 4) — TC-91's causal language exceeded its instrumentation. Characterization line 488 asserted 'TC-91 (a) IS TC-91 (b)' and 'a duplicate requires a second writer holding the WAL write lock across the worker commit'. CONFIRMED as an overclaim and REWRITTEN to the narrower, defensible claim across §0 item 4, §5.5 (restructured into 5.5.1 MEASURED / 5.5.2 HYPOTHESIS / 5.5.3 what would close it / 5.5.4 TC-57 uncertainty 3), §5.4's heading, §5.6 item 8, §6 item 6, §8 unsure-item 1 (PROMOTED to first), the tc91 module header, and the mechanism test's doc-comment. WHAT IS MEASURED AND KEPT: (1) the duplicate rate is CADENCE-SENSITIVE under this 1 ms embed / 1 ms write shape — 32.5/60 tight, exactly 0/60 at 25 ms spacing, 0/96 for one batch with no concurrent writer; (2) an externally held WAL write lock makes discarded worker commits INVISIBLE — 86.4/96 duplicates while `'failed'` terminals and `projection_failures` rows both read zero. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: that a duplicate REQUIRES that overlap, or that (a) is (b) in all cases. The reason is now stated in the doc as a durable finding in its own right: THERE IS NO DIRECT INSTRUMENTATION OF WORKER COMMIT FAILURES IN THE BASELINE DUPLICATE ARMS, BECAUSE THE DEFECT UNDER STUDY IS PRECISELY THAT THOSE FAILURES ARE DISCARDED by `let _ =` — i.e. TC-91 (b) IS THE REASON TC-91 (a) CANNOT BE CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT. That is a limit on what could be OBSERVED, not a proof of identity; the forced-lock arm supplies the holder EXTERNALLY, so it reproduces the mechanism and proves the blind spot but cannot attribute the baseline population. §5.5.3 names R-C as what converts the hypothesis into a measurement (the main reason it is recommended first), and §4 bar item 9 plus §5.6 item 8 now FORBID scoping a 0.8.21 fix against the unproven identity, citing TC-57 §0: the prior write-ups were confidently wrong about 517 and a fix would have shipped inert.

fix-3 ITEM 1 [determinism — the only round-5 finding with teeth] (codex §9 round 5) — live pin 3 was timing-sensitive AND sat in the DEFAULT merge gate. `tc90_transition_write_race.rs:995` started the blocker thread, slept a fixed 100 ms, and then ASSUMED the blocker held the WAL write lock. CONFIRMED BY READING: under loaded scheduling the writer can reach `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` before the blocker ever acquires the lock, and `elapsed >= HOLD / 2` then fails while the engine is behaving correctly. The fix-2 evidence (20 runs, 832-838 ms) measured the HAPPY path only; it does not bound the LOST-RACE path, which is exactly what a loaded CI box produces. It also made the design doc's 'the lock is HELD, not raced' framing (§3.4) untrue of pin 3's own setup. Given TC-72 (~1 workspace run in 3 already fails on plain `main`), a sleep-timed assertion in the merge gate is the wrong direction. FIXED AT THE ROOT RATHER THAN GATED, as the steward directed: the blocker now SIGNALS on a `std::sync::mpsc` channel AFTER its `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` has returned and it has written under the lock, and the main thread blocks on `recv_timeout(READY_TIMEOUT)` before it starts timing; `HOLD` begins at that same instant. The lock therefore genuinely IS held for the whole measured call — the property pins 1 and 2 get from being single-threaded — so the pin stays LIVE and honest and the §3.4 framing is now true of all four live targets instead of three. `READY_TIMEOUT` is 30 s and is NOT a timing assertion: it exists so a blocker that never starts fails LOUDLY instead of hanging the suite. INVENTORY UNCHANGED at 13 tests / 9 ignored / 4 live — nothing was gated, so neither §3.4 nor either module header needed a count change. RE-MEASURED N=10 after the rework: 10/10 green, pin 3 at 931-937 ms (a second confirming N=10: 932-937). The spread is 6 ms, the SAME as the sleep version — the rework did not tighten the happy path and was never meant to; what it removed is the UNBOUNDED path, which no number of quiet-machine runs can bound. Under a deliberate 24-way CPU load on a 24-thread box, 10 further runs stayed green at 934-941 ms, still more than double the 450 ms bound. The measured wait moved 834 -> ~935 ms for the expected reason (the 900 ms hold now begins when the writer does, instead of overlapping a 100 ms head start, plus the writer's own ~35 ms), so every stale 834 in the doc — §0 headline item 3, §3.3's pin table, §3.3's prose — was corrected rather than left to rot. `Mutex` import dropped (the `released` flag it guarded was write-only and is gone).

fix-3 ITEM 2 [residual overclaim] (codex §9 round 5) — the TC-91 module header still contradicted its own corrected body. Line 3 said the two defects 'share one mechanism' and line 66 said 'MEASURED ... and (a) turns out to BE (b)', both stronger than the hypothesis language at lines 92-103 of the SAME file and than design-doc §5.5.2. fix-4 ITEM 1 [the round-6 residual — CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION, path (a), no fallback needed] (codex §9 round 6, the ONLY finding left open; codex closed items 2/3/4 outright). The readiness signal introduced in fix-3 was correctly PLACED and READY_TIMEOUT is correctly a hang-guard, but at tc90_transition_write_race.rs:1021-1022 the holder called `ready_tx.send(())` and IMMEDIATELY began `sleep(HOLD)`. The window between the main thread's `recv_timeout` returning and `started = Instant::now()` was unguarded: a ~485 ms deschedule there released the lock before the measured `engine.write` began and `elapsed >= HOLD/2` would fail on a CORRECT engine. CONFIRMED BY READING before touching anything. FIXED with a two-phase handshake `ready` -> `ack` -> hold: the holder announces the lock and then WAITS; the main thread receives `ready`, takes `started = Instant::now()`, and ONLY THEN sends `ack`; the holder begins `sleep(HOLD)` on the ack. Because `started <= ack sent <= ack received = hold begins`, the lock is released no earlier than `started + HOLD`, and the measured call cannot return before that release because it needs the very lock the holder is sitting on. A main-thread stall before the ack only makes elapsed LARGER; a holder stall after it only extends the hold. Neither can shorten it. Both waits keep the 30 s READY_TIMEOUT hang-guard and `holder.join()` is now CHECKED so a panicking blocker surfaces as a panicking test rather than being swallowed by `let _ =`. The bound was NOT loosened and the pin was NOT gated.

The first draft of the TC-90 loop derived each transition's target state from the LOOP INDEX. pin3_rework.from: single readiness signal; the holder began sleep(HOLD) at the instant it signalled, leaving the main thread's recv_timeout -> Instant::now() gap unguarded
pin3_rework.to: two-phase handshake ready -> ack -> hold; the holder begins sleep(HOLD) only after the main thread has taken `started` and acknowledged
pin3_rework.soundness_argument: started <= ack sent <= ack received = hold begins, therefore release >= started + HOLD; and the measured engine.write cannot return before the release because it needs the same lock. Hence elapsed >= HOLD on every schedule. A main-thread stall before the ack only enlarges elapsed; a holder stall after it only extends the hold.
pin3_rework.hang_guards: READY_TIMEOUT (30 s) on BOTH waits; holder.join() now CHECKED (was `let _ =`) so a panicking blocker fails the test loudly
pin3_rework.load_shape: 24 spinning shell processes on a 24-thread box; load average 0.74 -> 5.66 across the run
pin3_rework.verdict: The loaded distribution is as tight as the quiet one (6 ms vs 7 ms), which is what a construction-sound bound should look like. Note explicitly recorded in §3.4: the happy-path numbers barely moved across all three shapes (sleep 832-838, signal 931-937, handshake 930-937), so NO amount of quiet-machine green distinguished them — only reading the ordering did. A measurement cannot show a race is absent; it can only fail to find it.
